4 Tbsp red wine vinegar, to serve
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Beetroot sprouts, to garnish
Linseed sprouts, to garnish

title: Ostrich fillets with pizziola sauce
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
a few sprigs of oregano, chopped
steps: Gently heat the oil and garlic in a wide pan. Remove once the garlic is browned
Add the steaks and brown on both sides. Remove, season and set aside
Add the tomato, oregano, wine, sugar and extra seasoning to the pan
Simmer over a medium heat, uncovered, for about 10 minutes or until reduced but chunky
Add the steaks and any juices. Turn the steaks in the sauce
Simmer for a few minutes, until heated through but still rare. Check seasoning. Serve with mashed gem squash

title: Mixed marrows & cottage cheese topping
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: 750 g thinly sliced Woolworths organic mixed marrows
4 baked & ready to serve sweet potatoes
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Place the marrows in a steamer over simmering water. Add some thyme and seasoning. Cover and steam for about 15 minutes, until just tender. Turn into a bowl and mix.
Serve with the topping and baked potatoes. If you like, garnish with chives and drizzle with canola oil.

title: Peanut Butter and Banana Smoothie
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 3 bananas, peeled and sliced diagonally into rounds
steps: Blend the milk with peanut butter and peeled bananas.
Fill your glass with the smoothie mixture, drizzle with honey and scatter over unsalted peanuts.

title: Easy Chicken Wraps
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: baby gem lettuce, rinsed and separated
steps: Rub chicken fillets with a little salt and dry chargrill on a ridged pan until cooked through.
Leave to rest, then slice and arrange on tortillas, along with dollops of mayonnaise, chopped spring onion, baby gem lettuce leaves and sliced avocado.
Roll up and serve with a squeeze of lime juice.

title: Spaghetti with meatballs
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 Tbsp fresh basil, chopped plus 4 sprigs for garnishing
salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Soak the bread in the milk and drain off any extra liquid. Mix together with all the ingredients and season to taste.
Roll into medium sized balls and place on a tray or dish. Cover and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Heat a little olive oil in a frying pan and cook over a medium heat until brown on both sides. Rather cook off in batches so that the pan is not to full.
If you are adding them to a sauce then donât overcook them as they will cook again in the sauce which should be on a gentle simmer for 10 minutes.

To make the sauce: Preheat oven to 180C and place tomatoes and leeks on a baking tray with the garlic and thyme, drizzle with olive oil. Roast for 30 minutes until soft then place in a saucepan together with remaining ingredients and simmer for 30 minutes.
Season to taste.

title: Three-Bean Macaroni Bake
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: 1 x 400 g can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
250 g macaroni, cooked until al dente and drained
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Drain all the beans, including the chickpeas, and mix with the Napoletana sauce.
You can buy Napoletana ready-made from Woolworths
Heat through. Mix with the well-drained, hot, cooked macaroni.
Check seasoning. Turn into an oiled baking dish. Sprinkle with parsley.
Spoon over the hot cheese sauce and sprinkle with Parmesan.
Slide under a hot grill to brown the top.

title: Sweet quinoa cooked in almond milk
author: Abigail Donnelly
steps: Combine the water and almond milk powder in a small saucepan. Simmer then add the quinoa.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the brown sugar and cinnamon stick.
Cook for a further 5 minutes, then serve with poached fruit and cinnamon sugar.

title: Peanut & vegetable rice-paper wraps
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: a few sprigs coriander leaves, to garnish
1 handful of mint, washed and torn
1 fresh red chilli, finely chopped for serving
steps: Steam the vegetables for 5 minutes, or until tender crisp.
While still warm, toss through the marinade.
Soak the fine noodles in boiling water for 10 minutes or until soft.
Drain very well then mix with the marinated vegetables. Add the salad onion.

title: Pan-Roasted Fish With Tomatoes & Olives
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: sea salt, plus extra to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Cut 800g fish fillet into pieces, score the skin and rub with sea salt and olive oil.
Heat a cast-iron pan and sear the fish, skin-side down, for 1 minute. Turn and cook for 1 minute.
Toss in  baby rosa tomatoes, pitted green olives, butter, crushed cloves garlic, chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Season, transfer to the oven and roast for 15 minutes.

title: Pumpkin, Cheese & Rosemary Muffins
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: freshly ground black pepper, to taste
60 g organic feta, cut into large cubes
steps: Preheat the oven to 190Â°C.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour and oats with the baking powder and salt. Mix in the Cheddar.
Blend the pumpkin with the eggs and olive oil and add to the bowl, mixing well with a fork. Add a twist or two of pepper.
Brush 6 extralarge muffin pans with oil, then spoon in the muffin mixture and bury a cube of feta in each one.
Sprinkle with Parmesan and tuck a sprig of rosemary into each. Bake for 20 minutes, or until golden and baked through.
Allow to stand for a few minutes before turning out. Serve warm, while the feta is still molten and gooey.

title: Moroccan lemon chicken on spinach
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
5 Tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
steps: Cut the chicken fillets in half then rub with the spice mix and olive oil. Thread onto bamboo skewers, soaked in water, then sear on a hot griddle pan for 1 to 2 minutes a side, or until cooked through but still tender. Season lightly.
Place a skewer or two on a serving of spinach or Swiss chard. Spoon over the lemon dressing and serve with the salsa.
To prepare the spinach/Swiss chard: Soak the leaves in a bowl of cold water. Drain. Pour over boiling water to cover and leave for 10 minutes. Drain and cool, then chop roughly.
Place in a saucepan over a medium heat, and cook, stirring now and again, for 10 to 15 minutes, or until the water has evaporated and the spinach is just tender.

title: Oat, Date & Coconut Muffins
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: 40 g desiccated coconut + extra for sprinkling
steps: Preheat the oven to 190Â°C.
Mix the oil and sugar together in a large bowl. Add the eggs and beat until frothy.
In a separate bowl, mix the flour with the baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, salt, spices, oats, trail mix and desiccated coconut.
Stir into the egg mixture. Add the yoghurt and mix until just combined, taking care not to overmix.
Grease a muffin pan and spoon in the mixture, filling each mould a third of the way.
Bury half a date in each filled muffin mould and sprinkle with coconut flakes.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until nicely risen and baked through. Allow to cool for a few minutes before removing from the muffin pan. Serve warm.

title: Chicken Soup
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 2 chopped onions, cut into thin rings
4 celery stalks, as is or thinly sliced to make curls, for serving
steps: Place all the ingredients into a saucepan except the pasta. Cover with cold water and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat down and let it simmer until the chicken meat falls off the bone. It will take about 1 hour.
Strain and reserve the liquid and spoon off any of the excess chicken fat.
Chop the chicken into small pieces and add back to the soup liquid.
Add the pasta and cook until al dente. Serve with crusty bread.

title: Shredded raw vegetables with eggs
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Mix the shredded vegetables (any mix of organic carrot, butternut, baby marrow, asparagus and baby corn) with the dressing and turn onto a serving plate
Add the spinach leaves and hard-boiled eggs
Drizzle with olive oil and season
Serve with the sauce on the side
For the dressing, mix together 3 T organic olive oil, flaky sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
For the sauce, mix together 1/3 cup organic mayonnaise, 1/3 cup organic plain yoghurt, 1 T chopped organic Italian parsley (optional)

title: Pumpkin tortillas
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 500g pumpkin, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Cook the pumpkin in a saucepan of boiling, salted water until tender, drain well
Mash the pumpkin using a fork and add the eggs, psyllium husk, nutmeg, chilli flakes and salt

Dust a work surface with coconut or almond flour and spoon equal quantities of mashed pumpkin onto the surface. Flatten the pumpkin until 2 cm thick using the palm of your hand. Ensure that each tortilla is completely covered in flour and dry and pliable
Heat a pan oven a medium heat and dry fry the tortillas for 3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown

title: Chicken and Corn Wraps
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: reserved marinade plus the pan juices
400 g free range skinless chicken breasts
steps: Mix the marinade ingredients together and marinate the chicken breasts for 15 to 30 minutes. Reserve the marinade.
Place the chicken in a cold non-stick pan, then bring to a medium heat. Once the chicken fillets are nicely browned, turn and brown the other sides.
Pour over the reserved marinade and bring to a bubble, stirring.
Remove from the heat and allow to cool. Slice the chicken thinly.

Cut the corn off the cobs and simmer in boiling water for a few minutes. Drain well and cool. Mix the dressing ingredients together then add the chicken and corn to the dressing, mix lightly and season to taste.
Warm the wraps slightly to make them pliable. Place a lettuce leaf or two on the middle of each wrap.
Add Â½ cup of the chicken-and-corn mixture.
Fold one side of the wrap over the filling, then fold over the ends and wrap to form an envelope.

title: Whole in One
author: TASTE
ingredients: 4 Tbsp canola oil, plus extra for greasing
steps: Preheat the oven to 180ÂºC.
Line each cup of a greased 6-cup muffin tray with 2 slices French bread, drizzle with olive oil and toast in the oven.
Fry the bacon and add the baby spinach. Stir until wilted and set aside.
Fry the onion and chives in the oil.
Mix with the bacon and spinach.
Beat 4 eggs and the fried ingredients and mix.
Spoon into the muffin tray and bake for 10 minutes.

title: Bulgur Wheat Flapjacks
author: Maranda Engelbrecht
ingredients: 1 cup bulgur wheat, soaked and loosened
fresh fruit of your choice (banana, guava etc.), for serving
steps: Combine the flour, egg and milk, until smooth. Add the sugar and bulgur wheat, and combine. The batter should be thick and slightly runny.
Add more flour or liquid if necessary. Heat a large, Teflon-coated pan until warm then add a little butter. Turn down the heat.
Add large spoonfuls of the batter and cook the flapjacks, two or three at a time, until golden brown on both sides.
Serve warm with maple syrup and fresh fruit.

title: Omelette with spring greens & beans
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Finely chop the dill, fennel, parsley and spring onions
Blanch the broad beans. Whisk the egg whites until soft peaks form and then fold in the egg yolks
Set aside some of the chopped herbs, then fold the rest into the egg mixture, along with the grated baby marrow. Season to taste
Heat the olive oil in a pan over a medium heat. Pour the mixture into the pan and cook briefly
Place the pan with the egg mixture under a hot grill until the top turns slightly golden in colour
Spoon over the cottage cheese, scatter with the remaining herbs and serve with the broad beans on the side
Serve on Low GI toast

title: Roast Chicken: Kids version
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: potatoes, roasted and crushed, for serving
green beans, sliced and blanched, for serving
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Combine the soy sauce and honey and generously spoon over the chicken.
Roast for 25 minutes or until the juices run clear.
Serve with crushed roast potatoes and sliced green beans.

title: Breakfast fruit tabbouleh
author: Maranda Engelbrecht
ingredients: 6 fresh dates, pitted and roughly chopped
6 pitted dates, dried and finely chopped
4 peeled and quartered guavas, peeled and sliced into wedges
steps: Bring the sugar and water or juice to a boil. Add all the fruit and poach for 3 to 5 minutes, to heat through.
Remove using a slotted spoon and place in a serving bowl with 250ml (1 cup) liquid poured over.
Simmer the juice for 10 minutes to reduce slightly to a light syrup.
Pour the syrup over the wheat and cover with a lid or clingfilm to absorb the liquid. Add a little more juice if necessary.
Keep covered for 30 minutes.
Remove the lid and loosen with a fork. Stir the wheat carefully into the fruit.
Serve topped with the pistachios and a drizzle of honey and yoghurt.

title: Mushrooms on French toast
author: Abigail Donnelly
steps: Lightly beat the eggs, then mix with the milk and a pinch of salt. Slice the farmhouse loaf into thick slices and dip into the batter.
Fry in the butter until golden on both sides. In a separate pan, cook the mushrooms in the olive oil until brown.
Add the balsamic vinegar and reduce until sticky. Spoon over the hot French toast and serve with grated Parmesan.

title: Asian chicken salad
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 2 cloves garlic, peeled and finely chopped
1/2 cup medium red onions, thinly sliced
steps: Fry the chicken mince, garlic  and ginger until golden and fragrant
Toss with the onion, cucumber, chilli, avocados, coriander, mint and a splash each of lemon juice, soya sauce and rice-wine vinegar

title: Spiced carrot & cashew salad
steps: Make a dressing by combining 1 t ground cumin, 1 clove crushed garlic, a good pinch of sea salt, Â¼ t cayenne pepper, 3 T sunflower oil, 3 T orange juice and 2 T lemon or lime juice
Peel 500g carrots then using the peeler shave the carrots into long ribbons and place into a mixing bowl
Mix with the dressing, then chill until ready to serve. To serve, turn onto a small platter and sprinkle with Â¼ cup roasted and roughly chopped cashew nuts. Garnish with fresh coriander

title: Butter Chicken Curry
author: Hannah Lewery
ingredients: 1 x 400g can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
4 free-range chicken breasts, cut into chunks
yoghurt or creme fraiche, for serving
steps: Gently fry a 70g sachet of butter chicken paste (available from Woolies) in 2 T oil until fragrant, for about 30 seconds.
Add a tin of canned cherry tomatoes or 100g fresh cherry tomatoes to the pan and stir before letting it simmer for 10 minutes.
Cut 4 free range chicken breast fillets into bite-sized chunks add to the pan with 6 baby marrows, sliced, and a 400g can of drained chickpeas. Simmer for 7-10 minutes until the chicken is cooked.
Serve hot with freshly chopped coriander, a swirl of cream or yoghurt, some atjar and fluffy basmati rice or ready-made rotis.

title: Banana & honey wheatgerm smoothie
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 2 mashed bananas, sliced thinly or cut into rounds
steps: Blend the rice milk, bananas, honey and wheatgerm in a food processor until smooth and thick.You can use any milk you like, including cow's or goat's milk. Or any of the alternative milks such as soya milk or almond milk
Serve as a quick breakfast or tea-time treat

title: Salmon steaks with cucumber salad
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: 500-700 g large potatoes, peeled and cubed
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Moisten the fish with oil and sear in a hot non-stick pan to seal and brown.
Season and place on a baking sheet lined with non-stick baking paper.
Before serving, bake at 180Â°C for 5 minutes.

title: The healthy caesar sandwich
ingredients: 4 large free range eggs, at room temperature
1 x 160 g pack baby gem lettuce, rinsed and separated
sea salt and pepper to taste
steps: In a frying pan over a high heat, toast the bread until lightly browned
While the toast is still hot, rub the slices with the peeled garlic and olive oil
Bring a medium-sized saucepan of water to a slow simmer and add the vinegar
Break the eggs into the water and poach them for 3 to 5 minutes (for a soft yolk), then drain
Toss the lettuce leaves with the lemon juice, anchovy fillets and grated pecorino
Divide the salad between the slices of toast and top each with a poached egg. Season to taste and serve.

title: Thai red tofu curry on rice pasta
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: 1 block tofu, cut into small squares
400 g tenderstem broccoli, sautÃ©ed or blanched
1 x 80 g sachet thai red curry paste
steps: Pat the tofu dry with paper towel and cut it into large cubes
Heat 6 tablespoons of coconut milk in a wide pan until bubbly
Stir in the curry paste and lemongrass and cook for about a minute, until fragrant
Add the vegetable stock, fish sauce, sugar and lime leaves. Bring to a boil
Add the tofu and simmer for a few minutes. Finally add the remaining coconut milk and vegetables
Simmer gently for a few minutes until tender, but crisp
To serve, sprinkle with coriander leaves and serve with rice noodles

title: Lemon chicken linguini
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat butter and olive oil in a saucepan.
Add sliced chicken breasts, lemon juice, lemon zest and crushed garlic, and pan-fry until golden.
Add fresh al dente linguini to the saucepan and toss until coated.
Stir through a handful of chopped parsley and season with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper.

title: Butternut, sweet potato and coconut pies
author: Abigail Donnelly
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C
In a saucepan over a medium heat, gently fry the chilli and garlic in the olive oil until fragrant and slightly softened
Add the butternut and sweet potato and fry for a further 5 minutes. Add the coconut milk, nutmeg and stock and leave to simmer for 10 to 15 minutes
Spoon the butternut and sweet potato broth into separate ovenproof bowls and season to taste
Cut four oversized sheets of phyllo pastry and lay one over each bowl
Secure in place with string, lightly brush with melted butter and sprinkle with pumpkin seeds
Bake for 10 minutes, or until the pastry is crisp and golden

title: Hot Turkish eggs with brown mushrooms
ingredients: small fresh red chilli, finely chopped for serving
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Fill a small saucepan three quarters full with water. Bring to a boil and add the vinegar.
Break each egg into a small bowl then carefully pour into the boiling water, cooking one at a time. For a soft egg, boil for 1 minute.
In a large saucepan, fry the mushrooms in the butter until golden brown. Serve each mushroom topped with a few spoons of yoghurt and an egg.
Sprinkle with the chopped chilli and garnish with rocket. Season to taste.

title: Paper-wrapped roast chicken
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
500 g portabellini and button mushrooms, or mushrooms of your choice
steps: Preheat the oven to 190Â°C.
Season the chicken inside and out. Season the cleaned mushrooms and moisten with oil.
Place as many mushrooms as you can, together with some of the thyme, inside the chicken cavity. Season the shallots and moisten with oil.
Place the chicken in the centre of a large sheet of oiled greaseproof paper. Tuck the remaining mushrooms, the shallots, garlic and some thyme underneath the chicken.
Moisten the skin of the chicken with olive oil. Wrap up in the paper and roast for 1Â¼ to 1Â½ hours, or until browned and very tender.
Serve with the roast mushrooms and shallots, topped with pan juices and with a green salad. Donât forget bread to mop up the juices.

title: Celery, apple and cucumber Asian slaw
steps: Grate cucumber, apples and celery stalks into long, thin strips.
Drizzle with lemon or lime juice, fish sauce and sesame seed oil.
Toss to coat and serve immediately.

title: Peaches & Plums with oats & pistachio
ingredients: 50 g pistachio nuts, shelled and roughly chopped
1 kg plums, quartered with pips removed
steps: Preheat the oven to 160Â°C.
Halve and stone the dessert peaches plums and place on a baking tray. In a clean mixing bowl, whisk the egg whites until soft peaks form. Add the caster sugar and whisk until stiff.
Fold in toasted rolled oats and chopped pistachio nuts. Top each peach and plum with meringue mix and 1 raspberry.
Bake for 15 minutes, or until the meringue is cooked and golden.

title: Baked fish with squashed tomato
author: Abigail Donnelly
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Tear four sheets of baking paper into 60 cm pieces and fold in half.
Place 1 hake fillet in the centre of each sheet and divide the squashed cherry tomatoes, garlic, olive oil, basil and fennel between them.
Season to taste and fold in the sides of the paper, then fold over to seal the parcels.
Bake on an oven tray for 10 to 15 minutes until cooked through, but succulent. Serve hot.

title: Zesty avocado salad with walnuts
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Run a vegetable peeler along the length of the celery sticks to create curls then transfer to a bowl of iced water.
Spoon out the avocado flesh, toss with the lemon juice and avocado oil and season to taste.
Place the avocado on a plate and top with the toasted walnuts and celery curls.
Garnish with the celery and mustard cress sprouts.

title: Crispy-skinned salmon
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
1/2 cup medium red onions, thinly sliced
1 juiced and zested lemon, cut into 8 slices
roasted Rosalina and baby vine tomatoes, selection
steps: Rub the salmon with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Fry, skin-side down, in a hot pan for 3 minutes, or until the skin is crispy, then turn and cook for a further 2 minutes until sealed but still a little pink in the middle.
Toss the salad ingredients with the lemon juice, dill and olive oil.
Serve the fish and salad with roasted tomatoes on the vine and blanched asparagus spears.

title: Salmon & avocado salad
author: Abigail Donnelly
steps: Boil extra-large free-range eggs* for 3 to 4 minutes. Peel and set aside.
Slice fillet lightly smoked trout into thin strips and arrange on a plate with fresh rocket and wedges of ripe avocado.
Squeeze over lemon juice and olive oil, season and serve with the eggs.

title: Salmon ceviche
author: Abigail Donnelly
steps: Thinly slice the salmon fillets, cover in lime juice and chill.
Remove the peel and pith of the ruby grapefruit and cut into segments.
Use a vegetable peeler to make curls out of a fennel bulb.
Serve salmon strips and grapefruit segments with chopped green chillies and fennel curls.

title: Nutty fruity breakfast
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 3 fresh figs,halved and served fresh or roasted
steps: Divide the fruit between two bowls.
Top each serving with a dollop of lemon yoghurt, drizzle with fruit juice and sprinkle with almonds.

title: Chicken with smashed peas & beans
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 4 chicken breast fillets, chopped into cubes
steps: Blanch the peas and broad beans. Using a fork, gently mash the peas and beans with the olive oil, mint and lemon juice. Season to taste.
Place the chicken breasts in a sieve and suspend over a saucepan of simmering water.
Cover and simmer for 5 minutes, turn and cook for a further 5 minutes.
To serve, place the peas in a bowl, slice the chicken breasts into pieces and place on top of the peas. Sprinkle with peppercorns and mint.

title: Marinated pork and plum salad
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 150 g watercress leaves, tough stalks removed
steps: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C
Leave the pork in the marinade for at least an hour, or overnight if more convenient
Remove the pork from the marinade, reserving the latter
Brown the pork all over in a nonstick pan, then place in a baking pan just large enough to take it and the reserved marinade, which should now be added
Roast for 20 minutes, basting once or twice
Once cooked, allow to cool, then slice. Mix the sliced pork with the cooking juices and spoon onto a platter or individual plates
After slicing the plums, add them and the watercress and drizzle with sesame oil

title: Quick chicken pot
author: Luke Dale-Roberts
ingredients: 200 g carrot, peeled and cut into chunks
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: In a pressure cooker, sautÃ© the onion, shallots and celery with the herbs, garlic and ginger in the butter and oil.
Add the chicken and brown lightly. Add the carrots, butternut, water and seasoning.
Cook at high pressure for 35 minutes.

title: Korma-spiced Indian curry
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 620 g ready-to-use cut vegetables, for roasting
canola oil, plus extra for greasing
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Toss the vegetables in the olive oil until coated then roast for 20 minutes.
Heat the canola oil in a saucepan with the korma spices or paste.
Add the chicken stock and simmer for 5 minutes.
Mix in the coconut milk, brown sugar and chilli.
Smash the dates in a pestle and mortar then add to the curry.
Simmer for 10 minutes then add the shredded chicken and roasted vegetables to warm through.
Serve steaming hot in deep bowls with fluffy rice and chopped fresh coriander. Season to taste.

title: Udon noodles in miso broth
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: thinly sliced fresh salmon fillet (150g â 200g each)
steps: Mix the miso to a paste with a little of the soup stock and set aside.
Heat the remaining stock with the noodles. Stir in the tofu and wakame and simmer until the wakame expands.
Whisk in the miso paste until smooth and heat through, but do not boil.
Add the salmon.
Garnish with spring-onion shreds.

title: Baked coconut & chicken curry
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Pour the rice into an ovenproof dish.
Arrange the chicken breasts and butternut chunks on top of the rice and drizzle with the olive oil.
Combine the coconut milk, coriander, lime zest and juice, cinnamon, korma spice, korma paste and chicken stock.
Pour the spicy coconut milk mixture over the chicken-andrice dish and season to taste.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the chicken is golden and tender.
Scatter with the toasted coconut shavings and serve.

title: Brunch stir fry with poached eggs
author: Maranda Engelbrecht
ingredients: a small handful fresh basil leaves, roughly chopped
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat oil in hot wok and add bacon. Cook until crispy, remove bacon and keep warm.
Stir-fry mushrooms and vegetable mixture for three to five minutes. Add tomatoes and basil. Turn the heat down, add bacon and stir through.

To poach eggs: Fill four cups a quarter full of hot water. Carefully break an egg into each cup and microwave on high for 30 seconds. Gently scoop eggs from water and serve on stir-fry. Season with salt and pepper and balsamic blaze.

title: Watercress & olive omelette
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Separate the eggs and whisk the whites to form soft peaks.
Whisk the yolks, then fold the whites into the yolks.
Add the butter to a small pan over a medium heat and, when hot, pour in the egg mixture.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, then flip to brown the reverse side.
Arrange the olives and watercress in the centre of the omelette and fold over.
Season to taste and serve immediately.

title: Granola, ricotta & yoghurt cups
author: Abigail Donnelly
steps: Add the frozen berries, icing sugar and berry juice to a bowl and blitz using a hand blender.
Pour the purÃ©ed mixture into a container and freeze until set.
Meanwhile, whip the ricotta, then fold in the yoghurt until smooth and dense.
Spoon into individual cups, dust half the top with crushed granola and top with a teaspoon of creamed honey and another of the berry "sorbet".
Serve immediately

title: Nicoise salad
author: TASTE
ingredients: 2 170g tin solid light meat tuna in water
steps: Mix the lemon juice, garlic and olive oil together, season to taste and set aside.
Place the potatoes and beans in a large bowl, add olives, tomatoes and spring onion and dress with half the salad dressing.
Arrange the tuna on top of the salad leaves with the eggs, and drizzle over the remaining dressing.

title: Roast pepper & bulgur wheat salad
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 1/2 lemon, cut into 8 slices for garnishing
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Halve red and yellow peppers and place on a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, scatter with sliced garlic and sea salt.
Roast for 30 minutes or until charred and slightly soft. Transfer the peppers, along with any juices, to a bowl, cover with clingfilm and allow to steam for a few minutes.
Remove the skins from the peppers and toss the flesh with olive oil, the juice of lemon, seasoning, finely chopped parsley and bulgur wheat, cooked according to package instructions.

title: Chicken pho bo
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 1 bok choy, cut into thin shards
steps: Heat the oil in a pan over a medium heat. Slice each chicken breast into 3 pieces and cook on both sides. Add the stock, bok choy and noodles and cook for 10 minutes.
Heat a pan over a medium heat and add the sesame seeds. Toss the seeds in the pan just until they darken slightly.

To serve, divide the noodles, bok choy and chicken between 4 bowls. Ladle over the chicken stock. Scatter over the toasted sesame seeds, spring onions, micro coriander, basil, mint and ginger. Serve the sambal oelek on the side.

title: Wholewheat spaghetti with tomato & basil
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 1 finely sliced red chilli, finely chopped
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook the spaghetti in rapidly boiling water until al dente and drain.
Warm the olive oil in a pan over a medium to low heat.
Pan-fry the  garlic and chilli until fragrant, then add to the pasta.
Squeeze the whole tomatoes over the pasta, allowing the juices to seep in.
Tear the basil leaves into the pasta, add the cherry tomato halves, olives and caperberries and mix well to combine.
Break the mozzarella into large chunks and scatter over the pasta.
Season to taste, add a glug of olive oil and serve immediately.

title: Spiced pork fillet with orange salad
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 190Â°C.
Trim the pork if necessary. Moisten with olive oil then sear in a pan over a high heat.
Transfer to a baking dish large enough to just hold the pork. Mix the remaining ingredients together and pour over the pork.
Bake for 15 minutes, or until cooked through but still moist.
Serve with the orange salad.

title: Raspberry & ricotta whip
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp sugar for the egg whites
steps: Mix the ricotta cheese and Greek yoghurt, then set aside.
Peel and chop the mango and divide between four glasses.
Spoon the pulp the granadillas on top of the mango, followed by the ricotta-and-yoghurt mixture.
Blend the raspberries with the sugar and spoon over the tops.

title: Poached breakfast pear with honey
author: Maranda Engelbrecht
ingredients: 3 pears, peeled, cored & cut into wedges
steps: Steam the pears in a steamer until they start to soften. Using a sharp knife, slice through carefully.
Sprinkle with some of the oats and seeds then plate.
Serve the yoghurt and remaining oats and seeds on the side. Drizzle with the honey.

title: Gingered sweet potato soup with cashews
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 400 g sweet potato, cooked and pureed
45 ml fresh coriander, leaves picked from stalks
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Melt the butter and oil in a large pan. Gently cook the leeks, ginger, chilli and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato and stock. Cover and simmer until the potato is soft.
Add the coconut milk and coriander. Blend until smooth.
To make the soy cashews, toss the nuts in soy sauce and roast at 180ÂºC for 15 minutes.
Season the soup and serve it with the soy cashews.

title: Chickpea & cashew curry
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: 2 x 400 g can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1 finely sliced red chilli, finely chopped
1/2  cup, coasely chopped and roasted cashew nuts, to serve
steps: Soften the onion in 1 or 2 tablespoons of peanut oil.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and spices for barely a minute until fragrant, and then stir in the coconut milk and bring to a bubble.
Add the drained chickpeas, chilli and a little salt and stir.
Reduce the heat and simmer for about 15 minutes.
Check seasoning. Serve over steamed rice, sprinkled with cashews and coriander leaves.

title: Carrot roll with sweet cardamom
ingredients: 70 g flour, plus extra for dusting
a pinch cardamom pods, cracked open
steps: Preheat the oven to 180ÂºC.
Separate eggs then beat the yolks with  caster sugar, until pale and thick.
In a separate bowl, sift cake four, cinnamon, nutmeg and  allspice. Add the egg yolks and a large carrot, grated.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add  golden syrup until the egg whites are stiff .
Fold the egg-white mixture into the carrot mixture. Carefully spoon the batter into a lined and greased 30 x 20 x 3cm-deep baking tray, then bake for 15 to 20 minutes, or until golden brown.
Remove from the oven then quickly turn out on baking paper sprinkled with caster sugar. Roll up like a Swiss roll and allow to cool.
To make the filling, coarsely grate 2 medium-sized carrots then place in a small saucepan. Add milk then simmer slowly, until the liquid has evaporated.
Add clarified butter and fry until the carrot mixture starts to brown. Add caster sugar or  honey and finely ground cardamom seeds.
Allow to cool then add fat-free Ayrshire yoghurt.
Open the roll onto a flat surface then spread with the carrot filling.
Roll up carefully, dust with caster sugar and serve sliced.

title: Parsnip & gorgonzola soup
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1 cup low- fat or soya cream
steps: Heat a little olive oil in a deep frying pan. Add sliced onion and cook for 2 minutes. Add parsnips and stock, bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer parsnips until soft.
Add cream and half the gorgonzola and stir through. Blend or process until smooth. Return to saucepan and reheat gently.
Season with black pepper. Garnish with the remaining cheese.
On the side: Wrap a roasted parsnip and a cheese straw in a slice of fiocco or proscuitto.

title: Baked ostrich meatballs on turnip mash
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 190Â°C.In a saucepan over a low heat, gently soften the onion in the oil. Stir in the garlic.
Crumble the bread and soak it in the stock. Mash together and allow to cool. Mix with the beaten egg, onion and garlic, and mince. Season to taste.

Form into 10 to 12 tennis ballsized rounds and coat with flour. Place in an oiled baking pan, cover with the sauce and bake for 30 minutes or until just cooked and nicely coloured. Garnish with parsley.

title: Beef knuckle stew on parsnip mash
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 4 large carrots, peeled and finely chopped
1 x 400 g woolworths ready-made chicken gravy packet
1 tin butter beans, soaked overnight and drained
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Place a large, heavy-bottomed saucepan over a medium heat. Add the olive oil, garlic, carrot and onion, then gently sweat, without colouring, until soft.
Add the beef knuckle then lightly brown on all sides. Pour over the beef stock and red wine, and slowly simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the gravy and butter beans then simmer for another 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the flavours infuse.

Cut the parsnips into cubes then add to a saucepan of boiling salted water. Cook until just tender, then drain and mash slightly, adding small amounts of cream until a smooth texture forms. Using a spoon, push the mashed parsnip through a sieve then keep warm.
In a saucepan, heat the vegetable oil until hot. Add the grated horseradish then fry until crisp and golden. Drain on a paper towel.
Divide the creamed parsnip among serving dishes, add a generous serving of warm beef-knuckle stew then sprinkle over crisp, golden shreds of horseradish. Season to taste.
For a slightly different texture, use cannellini beans instead of butter beans. Serve with steamed fine green beans.

title: Spicy fish pie with tomato & cauli mash
ingredients: 100 ml low- fat or soya cream
salt and white pepper to taste
steps: Combine all the ingredients in a food processor or blender to a smooth paste
Divide the paste into two, using separate bowls. Use the first bowl, and smear the fish lightly on both sides.  Keep the remaining paste on the side

Heat a little butter in a Teflon coated pan until warm. Sear each type of fish, separately on both sides until golden brown. Try to keep the fish whole. Do not overcook the fish; it is still going to be cooked in the oven
Remove from the heat and keep on the side. Once cooled down remove any visible skin of the fish, by just peeling it off from the one side to the other
Smear the remaining paste over the best looking side of the fish.
Use a small sharp paring knife and slice a cross on the bottom of the tomato, just through the skin and not into the flesh
Dunk the tomatoes with skin for 1 minute in boiling water
Remove and cool down slightly
Use the sharp paring knife and pull the skin from the tomato
Slice the tomatoes in half and remove the pips by using a spoon
Slice the tomatoes in small equal size blocks
Pre heat the oven grill
Use a chefâs knife and slice carefully vertically through the cauliflower
Slice three 5mm slices cauliflower like a slice of bread and place on a baking tray.
Smear on both sides with butter and place under grill. Keep the remaining cauliflower for the mash
Cook for 5- 10 minutes until golden brown and turn over
Remove from oven and keep on the side
Slice cauliflower and onion into chunks
Place into a deep saucepan and add a little boiling water just to reach the bottom quarter of the cauliflower and onion. Steam until the cauliflower start to soften
Remove excess water and add cream and butter. Mash or place in a blender. Add more cream if necessary
Season with salt and pepper to taste.  Divide the mixture into two

title: Seared ostrich with griddled pap
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1 x 250 g jar ginger and Peppadew relish
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Dry fry the bacon rashers in a nonstick pan over a high heat until crisp. Reserve the fat for later.  Cut the bacon into small bits and mix with the warmed stiff pap and parsley.
Place the pap on a clean surface and press down to a thickness of 2 cm. Cut into rounds using a cookie cutter and brush with melted butter. Fry in a griddle pan.

Heat the reserved bacon fat in a nonstick pan and rub the garlic, thyme and seasoning into the ostrich. Pan-fry for 3â4 minutes on each side for rare â take care not to overcook it. Serve with the pap and relish.
To make the relish, sautÃ© the onion and garlic in the olive oil for 2 minutes. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the ginger-and-Peppadew relish. Season to taste and keep warm.

title: Warm roasted carrot salad with yoghurt
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pre-heat the oven to 180Â°c.
Place the carrots in a roasting dish and drizzle over the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and place in the oven.
Allow to roast for 35 minutes or until slightly caramelised and just cooked through.
To serve, combine the yoghurt, lemon juice, zest and seasoning and mix well.
Spread the yoghurt on a serving plate and top with the roasted carrots.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and micro rocket leaves before serving.

title: Roasted shallot tart with goat's cheese
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pre-heat the oven to 150Â°c.
Peel and halve the shallots then toss with the olive oil, Balsamic, salt & pepper.
Place in a roasting dish and place in the oven.
Allow to roast slowly for 45 mins â 1hour until they are soft and caramelised.
Remove the shallots from the oven then turn the heat up to 180Â°c.
Place the thawed pastry on a baking tray and lightly score a 1cm border around the edge of the pastry.
Place the roasted shallots and crumbled goatâs cheese inside the border then brush the border with the beaten egg yolk.
Place the tart into the oven and allow to bake for 20-25 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden brown.
Remove from the oven, scatter over the micro leaves and drizzle with honey before serving.

title: Romanesco & bacon linguini
ingredients: 2 small heads romanesco, cut into florets
1/2 lemon, cut into 8 slices for garnishing
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Pre-heat the oven to 200Â°c.
Toss the romanesco florets with the olive oil, salt and pepper and place in a roasting dish.
Place in the oven and allow to roast for 20-25 minutes until they start to caramelise.
In the meanwhile, heat a large, non-stick frying pan over high heat and fry the bacon until crisp.
Add the roasted romanesco to the pan and fry for another 3-5 minutes with the bacon.
Pour in the cream and lemon juice and season to taste.
Toss the sauce with the cooked pasta and serve with a generous grating of Parmesan cheese.

title: Onion Bhajis with buttermilk
author: TASTE
ingredients: 2 cups buttermilk, plus extra for serving
steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan. Place the flour into a bowl with the garam masala, turmeric and salt.
Add 1 cup buttermilk and mix to combine. Slice the onions into rings and then in half. Coat in the batter and deep fry in the oil until golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper.
Mix the remaining buttermilk with the chutney and serve with the bhajis.

title: uJeqe - Steamed Zulu bread
author: TASTE
ingredients: 410 g can chakalaka, warmed, for serving
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, water, yeast and salt to form a very loose dough. Knead the dough for 10 minutes by gripping it and slapping it against the side of the mixing bowl. Place the dough into a clean, greased plastic shopping bag and knot closed. Place in a warm area for about 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Place a steamer over a saucepan of simmering water. Place the bag containing the dough inside the steamer and steam for 1 hour, or until a skewer inserted comes out clean. Serve with the chakalaka.

title: Biltong and bacon dip
author: TASTE
ingredients: 4 Tbsp canola oil, plus extra for greasing
10 slices bacon, chopped and fried until crispy, to serve
steps: Heat the canola oil in a pan over a medium heat. Roughly chop the bacon and fry until crisp. Drain on kitchen paper.
In a food processor, blend the cream cheese, 5 T biltong sprinkle and the Dijon mustard until well combined.
Spoon into a serving dish and scatter over the crispy bacon. Garnish with the remaining biltong, powder. Serve with the three cheese straws.

title: Pap pizza
author: Siba Mtongana
ingredients: 200 g Woolworths basil pesto, feta and sundried tomato dip
150 g tenderstem broccoli tips, half raw and blanched
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 220Â°C. In a medium-sized saucepan, bring the water and salt to a rapid boil. Add half the maize meal, reduce the heat to medium and cook, covered, for 8 minutes. Stir the mixture and add the remaining maize meal, a little at a time, stirring and beating it against the sides of the saucepan with the back of the wooden spoon.
This should take about 5 minutes. Reduce the heat further, cover and cook for 10â15 minutes. Add the butter and mix. Cool slightly.

Flatten the cooled pap into a pizza pan, creating a thin base. Mix the sundried tomato and feta part of the dip with the sweet chilli sauce and spread over the pap base. Scatter over the chorizo, onion, broccoli, a spoonful of the basil pesto and the Parmesan. Season to taste and bake for 10 minutes, or until the cheese has melted. Serve warm.

title: Mini vetkoek with mince
author: TASTE
ingredients: 360 g flour, plus extra for dusting
200 g sugar for the egg whites
canola oil, plus extra for greasing
2 chopped onions, cut into thin rings
1 finely sliced red chilli, finely chopped
4 potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes
125 ml apricot jam, melted, plus extra for serving
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: To make the dough, combine the dry ingredients in a large bowl. Add the water, a little at a time, mixing with a wooden spoon until a wet dough forms.

Knead in the bowl for 5 minutes or until the dough springs back after being pressed with your finger. Cover the bowl with cling wrap and allow the dough to rise for 30â45 minutes or until doubled in size.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan and fry the onions, red chilli and garlic for 2â3 minutes.
Add the mince and Cape Malay curry powder to the pan and cook until browned.
Add the chopped tomatoes to the mince.
Pour in the beef stock and simmer over a medium heat for 5 minutes, then add the potatoes.
Cover with a lid and simmer for 10â15 minutes, stirring at regular intervals.
Add the apricot jam and coriander and season to taste. Add the peas.
Once the potatoes are cooked through, adjust the seasoning and remove from the heat.
Heat the canola oil for frying the vetkoek in a separate saucepan over a medium heat. Knock the dough back and divide into 16 equalsized vetkoeks.
Gently drop 4 vetkoek into the oil and cover the saucepan with a lid. This allows the vetkoek to partially steam while frying.

Cook for 2 minutes, or until golden on one side, then turn and cook the other side. When cooked through and golden, remove the vetkoek from the oil using a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Cook the remaining vetkoek in the same way.
Serve the mini vetkoek with the savoury mince and garnish with fresh coriander.

title: Traditional snoek bobotjie
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin seeds, toasted and crushed
410 g can chopped and peeled tomatoes
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Cut the snoek into large pieces, place in a saucepan of boiling water and simmer gently until cooked, 5â10 minutes. Drain, allow to cool, then flake the fish, removing the bones.

Place the bread in a bowl, pour over 1/2 cup milk and leave to soak. In a pan over a medium heat, gently fry the onion in the oil, then add the ginger, garlic, curry leaves (if using), spices and curry powder. Fry for 2 minutes, then add the tomato. Cook until reduced and the mixture starts to thicken.

Squeeze the excess milk from the bread and break it up into large chunks. Sprinkle over the smoke snoek flakes and add the spicy sauce. Stir until combined, then transfer to a baking dish and add the lemon or bay leaves and cassia sticks. Beat the eggs with the remaining milk and pour over the fish.
Bake for 40â45 minutes, or until the custard is set and the edges browned.

title: Easy, spicy Biryani
author: TASTE
ingredients: 2x15 g sachets Woolworths pilau rice spice blend
yoghurt, tomato and coriander sambal, for serving
steps: Heat the olive oil in a pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook until brown and soft. Add the raisins, pilau rice spice blend, turmeric and chicken, coating the chicken in the spice and browning. Add a little water if it sticks.
Once the chicken is cooked, add the rice and toss through, coating it in the spice. Season with salt to taste.
Garnish with the pomegranate rubies and serve with the yoghurt, tomato and coriander sambal.

title: Braaied Yellowtail with apricot
author: TASTE
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
6 Tbsp apricot jam, melted, plus extra for serving
1/2 lemon, cut into 8 slices for garnishing
steps: Drizzle the outside of the fish with olive oil, then season to taste.
Braai, without turning, over medium coals for 5 minutes on each side.
Brush the glaze onto the fish and continue cooking, turning often so the glaze doesnât burn.

title: Pickled pear salad with fish cake
author: TASTE
ingredients: 4 Ripe pears, peeled, quartered and pips removed
steps: Place the pears, red wine vinegar, cinnamon and sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer for 15â20 minutes, or until the fruit is soft and pink in colour. Set aside to cool.
Fill a large saucepan to three-quarters with water and bring to the boil. Add the potatoes and cook until soft. Drain and allow to cool slightly.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and fry the onions, garlic and chilli flakes.
Using a large metal spoon, mash the potatoes in a bowl, then add the onion mixture.
Break up the smoked snoek fillets and add to the mashed potatoes with the parsley, lemon juice and zest. Season to taste.
Heat the canola oil in a pan. Shape the snoek mixture into 8â10 medium-sized fish cakes.
Coat each fish cake in flour, then dip it into the beaten egg. Remove from the egg mixture and roll in the panko breadcrumbs.
Fry the fish cakes in batches until golden brown and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper.
Serve with the pickled pear salad.

title: Crustless cardamom milk tart
steps: Preheat the oven to 160Â°C.
Combine the egg yolks, sugar and butter and beat until pale and creamy.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt and, together with the milk, fold into the sugary egg mixture.
Add the vanilla paste, cardamom and naartjie zest and fold in the beaten egg whites until combined. .
Line a  20 cm round baking tin with baking paper and pour in the mixture.
Sprinkle with a good dusting of cinnamon sugar, then bake for 1 hour, or until almost set with a lovely golden crust. Remove from the oven and leave to cool, then refrigerate until set.

title: Afrikaans koeksisters
author: TASTE
ingredients: 300 g sugar for the egg whites
280 g flour, plus extra for dusting
1/2 tsp sea salt, plus extra to taste
4 Tbsp butter, plus extra, melted, for the tart base
steps: Sign in/Register

title: Traditional malva pudding
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1 Tbsp apricot jam, melted, plus extra for serving
steps: Preheat the oven to 190Â°C. Place the caster sugar, eggs and apricot jam in a large mixing bowl and beat until pale and fluffy. In a separate bowl, sift the cake flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt, then whisk to incorporate.

Melt the butter in a small saucepan over a low heat, then stir in the vinegar and milk, mixing until combined. Add the dry mixture to the sugar-andegg mixture and combine. Add the buttery milk mixture and whisk until a smooth batter forms.

Grease a large ovenproof dish and pour in the mixture. Bake for 35â40 minutes, or until golden in colour and a skewer inserted comes out clean. Pour the sauce over the warm pudding and serve with custard.

To make the sauce, place all the ingredients (cream, butter, treacle sugar and sherry)  in a saucepan over a medium heat and stir until the butter is melted, the sugar dissolved and the sauce heated through.

title: Malay koesisters
author: TASTE
ingredients: 300 g flour, plus extra for dusting
55 g sugar for the egg whites
a pinch of sea salt, crushed, plus extra for topping
300 g sugar for the egg whites
500 g desiccated coconut + extra for sprinkling
steps: Boil the potato in its jacket. While itâs still hot, peel and mash until smooth.
Sift the flour, 50 g sugar and salt. Stir in the spices and naartjie peel or zest. Rub in 4 T oil with the potato to form a crumbly mixture.
Combine the milk and water, then add the yeast and remaining sugar and mix to dissolve. Add the milk mixture and egg to the dry ingredients. Mix well to form a very soft and sticky dough.
Moisten your hands with a little oil and rub them over the dough, cover and set aside for 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
Generously coat your hands in oil and knock down the dough. Place on a well-oiled surface, and divide into 12 to 16 balls. Again, allow the dough to double in size (30â40 minutes).
Heat the remaining oil in a large saucepan and fry the koeksisters until golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
Submerge the koeksisters in the syrup and place over a low heat to soak for at least 20 minutes. Remove from the syrup and roll in the coconut mixture. Serve warm.
To make the syrup, dissolve the sugar in the water over a low heat. Once dissolved, bring the syrup to a boil and cook for 5 minutes.
To make the coconut coating, place the coconut, dried naartjie peel and cinnamon in a pan and toast until golden brown. Allow to cool, then add the fresh naartjie zest.

title: Pavlova with fresh raspberries & cream
ingredients: 250 ml (1 cup) low- fat or soya cream
steps: Pre-heat the oven to 150Â°c and line a baking tray with baking paper.
In  a clean, dry bowl, whip the egg whites until light and frothy then slowly start adding the sugar (300 g) whilst continuously whisking.
Continue whisking until the egg whites are thick and glossy (stiff peak stage).
Form the meringue on the lined baking tray into a large pavlova.
Place in the oven and immediately turn the heat down to 100Â°c.
Allow to bake for 1h30 mins until crisp but still marshmallowy inside then switch off the oven and allow to cool completely inside.
When the pavlova is cool, whip the cream with the caster sugar (30 g) and vanilla until soft peaks form then top the pavlova with the whipped cream.
Top with the fresh raspberries and serve.

title: Butter cookies with quick raspberry jam
ingredients: 1 x 300 g vanilla butter cookie mix
steps: To make the jam, combine all the ingredients in a small saucepan then allow to simmer for 10-15 minutes until thick.

To check if the jam is ready, place a teaspoon-full onto a plate and allow to cool for 30 seconds. Drag your finger through the jam, if the edges donât âbleedâ into one another, the jam is ready.
Remove from the saucepan and transfer to a sterilised jar.
Allow to cool completely before storing in the fridge for up to 1 month.
To make the cookies, pre-heat the oven to 180Â°c and line 2 baking sheets with baking paper.
Make the cookies following the package instructions.
Cut shapes of your choice out of the rolled out dough, ensuring you have an even number of cookies to make sandwiches. Cut a smaller shape out of half of the cookies to allow the jam to peek through.
Bake the cookies until they are golden brown then remove and allow to cool completely before sandwiching with the raspberry jam and dusting with icing sugar.

title: Chocolate truffle and raspberry tart
ingredients: 250 g flour, plus extra for dusting
240 g Dark chocolate, chopped and melted
100 ml low- fat or soya cream
steps: To make the crust, combine the butter (125 g), flour and caster sugar in the bowl of a food processor.
Pulse until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs then add the egg yolk.
With the motor running, add the water until the dough comes together in a ball.
Tip the dough onto a floured surface and form into a disc.
Wrap the dough in clingwrap and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Pre-heat the oven to 180Â°c.
Roll the chilled dough into a large circle then transfer to a quiche/pie dish.
Line the pastry with baking paper and fill with baking weights (dry beans or rice work well) and place in the oven.
Bake for 10 minutes before removing the weights and baking paper then bake for another 10 minutes until crisp and golden.
Remove from the oven and allow to chill completely.
In the meanwhile, melt the chocolate and cream together until smooth and glossy.
Beat in the butter (30 g) and allow the truffle mixture to cool for a few minutes.
Put the raspberries into the empty tart case then pour over the truffle mixture.
Place in the fridge until the truffle filling is set then serve with extra raspberries.

title: Sesame & chilli fried noodles with pork
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1 ginger root, peeled and cut into julienne strips
400 g Hokkien noodles, soaked in water
1 fresh red chilli, finely chopped for serving
steps: Rub the fillet with mustard.
Heat the butter in a saucepan and gently fry fillet until golden brown and cooked while turning on all sides.

title: Double steak burger with parsnip crisps
author: TASTE
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: 500 g extra lean beef mince
1 medium onion,chopped /
5 ml coriander, ground
60 ml tomato paste
2 garlic cloves
15 g fresh coriander, chopped
60 ml breadcrumbs
60 ml fruit chutney
1 egg
5 ml lemon zest
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
butter or oil for frying

title: Traditional Malay samosas
author: TASTE
steps: SautÃ© the chopped onion in a medium pot until softened.
Add the garlic and ginger and ground spices and cook for 2-3 min.
Add the mince and cook for 10 min until cooked through and browed.
Once the filling is cool, place 1 T of filling onto a pastry rectangle and roll as directed below.
Deep fry in hot oil until golden, about 3 to 5 minutes

title: Citrus and ginger milk tart
ingredients: 2 tbsp sugar for the egg whites
3 Tbsp cornflour, mixed with 2 1/2 Tbsp cold water
steps: In a food processor blend the ginger biscuits, place in a bowl with the melted butter and mix until combined and compact.
Line the tins you will be using with the ginger biscuit mixture and set aside.
Whisk the eggs, corn flour, flour and sugar together in a bowl to form a thick paste.

Heat the milk, butter, zest, ginger and vanilla, stirring continuously. Remove the milk mixture, strain and add to egg mixture. Return to the heat, whisking until the mixture thickens, for about 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat when the mixture coats the back of a spoon and divide among the ginger biscuit crusts and chill in the refrigerator for 40 minutes before serving.

title: Raspberry frozen yoghurt & cones
author: TASTE
ingredients: 65 g sugar for the egg whites
400 g cake flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Heat the milk and sugar over a medium heat until the sugar has dissolved. Cool for 30 minutes.
Puree the raspberries using a hand-blender, then add to the milk-and sugar mixture with the yoghurt and vanilla extract.
Pour into an ice cream machine and churn for 15â20 minutes, or until thick. Place in a container and freeze.

title: Mustard, artichoke & potato salad
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook the potatoes in a saucepan of rapidly boiling water until tender, then drain.
Slice into rounds.
Toss in the whole-grain mustard, lemon juice and olive oil until coated.
Cut the artichokes in half and scatter over the potatoes.
Top with the red onion slices and baby leaves.
Season to taste and serve.

title: Creamy summer potato salad
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 8 large potatoes, cooked, peeled and chopped into chunks
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 180ÂºC.
Grease the grid of a cooling rack with the olive oil before draping with the slices of Serrano ham. Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, or until crisp. Allow to cool.
Place a large saucepan of salted water over a high heat and add the potatoes. Bring to a boil and cook until tender, but still firm. Drain and cut into large cubes.
In a bowl, mix together the horseradish sauce, mayonnaise, sliced celery and celery leaves. Season then add the potato cubes and mix until evenly coated.
Place a Serrano-ham wafer on each plate and top with the potato salad.
Using a fine grater, grate the radishes over the salad and finish with a good crack of black pepper.
Crumble over the remaining Serrano ham.

title: Potato salad with bacon
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: a pinch of sea salt, crushed, plus extra for topping
400 ml canola oil, plus extra for greasing
steps: Rinse the baby potatoes, place in a saucepan and just cover with water. Bring to the boil and cook for 5 to 10 minutes, or until tender. Drain and slice in half.
Place egg yolks, English mustard and salt in a mixing bowl.
Whisk until combined and slowly add the canola oil in a thin stream, whisking continuously until the mixture is fairly stiff.
Whisk in the red wine vinegar.
Season and toss the potatoes in the mayonnaise.
Serve topped with sliced spring onions and crispy bacon pieces.

title: Braaied lemon & herb chicken
author: Abigail Donnelly
steps: Mix olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice and chopped black olives, then carefully stuff under the skin of the chicken along with a few sprigs of thyme and rosemary.
Grill over hot coals for 50 to 60 minutes, or until the skin is crispy and the juices run clear.

title: Pap layered with peppers & mushrooms
ingredients: 2 cloves garlic, crushed and roughly chopped
1 of each red, yellow and green peppers, diced
sea salt and pepper to taste
1-2 cups cheddar, grated for the top
steps: Pre-heat the oven to 180Â°c.

To make the pap, heat the water in a large pot then whisk in the maize meal. Add the salt and allow to come to a simmer then turn down the heat and cover the pot. Allow to cook very gently for 10-15 minutes until all the water has been absorbed.
Stir in the butter and cheese and set aside.
In a large frying pan, saute the vegetables until soft and golden brown then pour in the chopped tomatoes.
Season to taste.
To assemble the âpaptertâ, place half of the cooked pap in the bottom of an oven-proof dish. Top with the vegetables then add the remaining pap.
Top with the grated cheddar and place in the oven.
Allow to bake for 10-15 minutes until the cheese has melted and the tart is golden brown.
Remove from the oven and allow to stand for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Rump steaks with mustard butter
author: Abigail Donnelly
ingredients: 2 tsp sea salt, plus extra to taste
steps: Combine all the ingredients (except the rump steaks) for the butter, roll into a cylinder, cover with clingfilm and refrigerate.
Place a soaked braai plank on the open flames. When it starts to smoke, place the rump on the planks and brown on both sides. Place a knob of mustard butter on each steak and allow to melt.

title: Spicy chakalaka
ingredients: 1 of each red, yellow and green peppers, diced
2 tsp sugar for the egg whites
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: In a large saucepan, saute the onion in olive oil until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and peppers and saute for a further 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, paprika, chilli flakes and sugar then turn down the heat and allow to simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until the vegetables are soft but still holding their shape.
Season to taste then serve.

title: Harissa & thyme marinade
steps: Combine all the ingredients in a bowl and mix well. Alternatively, combine in a jar and shake well.
Use to marinade lamb, chicken or beef and marinade for up to 24 hours before cooking.

title: Braaied snoek with moskonfyt
author: Suzi Holtzhausen of Gaaitjie in Paternoster
ingredients: coarse salt & freshly ground white pepper
125 ml moskonfyt, plus a little extra
1 handful, fresh and torn basil leaves, finely chopped
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Gut, trim, debone and butterfly the snoek. Open out the fish and season both the skin and flesh with salt and white pepper.

Combine the juice, miso paste, moskonfyt and half the olive oil and spread over the fish, rubbing into the flesh. Allow to stand for 30 minutes, then brush the remaining olive oil over both sides of the fish.
Line a fish grill with the sea-marsh grass and lay the fish on top. Cover with the remaining grass and grill over medium to hot coals, about 8 minutes a side.
Drizzle with the extra moskonfyt while cooking. Remove from the grill and scrape off the grass.

title: Fresh chilli and garlic marinade
ingredients: 2 cloves garlic, peeled and finely chopped
2  Tbsp red wine vinegar, to serve
steps: Combine all the ingredients in a bowl/jar and mix well.
Use to marinade chicken (up to 24 hours) or prawns (up to 2 hours) before cooking.

title: Zesty lemon, herb & garlic marinade
ingredients: 4 Tbsp fresh mixed herbs of your choice (for example: rosemary, parsley, thyme and sage)
steps: Combine all the ingredients in a bowl/jar and mix well.
Use to marinade chicken, fish, pork or vegetables for up to 24 hours before cooking.

title: Homemade BBQ sauce
ingredients: 2  Tbsp red wine vinegar, to serve
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Combine all the ingredients in a saucepan and bring to the boil.
Allow to simmer for 10-15 minutes until the sugar has dissolved and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Transfer to a bowl/jar and allow to cool completely before using to marinade chicken, ribs or steak.

title: Braai Bruschetta
author: TASTE
ingredients: 8 thinly sliced Woolworths organic mixed marrows
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Toss 8 thinly sliced Woolworths organic mixed marrows and 1 thinly sliced exotic brinjal in 2 T olive oil with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste.
Chargrill the vegetables on a grid over hot coals.
Halve 1 Woolworths Heat & Eat ciabatta lengthways, brush with olive oil and chargrill, cut side down, on the grid.
Top with charred veggies and a generous dollop of Woolworths basil pesto.

title: Chicken tapas
ingredients: 2 tsp fresh coriander, leaves picked from stalks
60 ml cornflour, mixed with 2 1/2 Tbsp cold water
8 fresh dates, pitted and roughly chopped
a pinch sea salt, plus extra to taste
2 chicken breast fillets, chopped into cubes
200 ml fresh pineapple, freshly squeezed from 8-10 pineapples

title: Braaied lamb chops with bean mash
author: Phillippa Cheifitz
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
