title: Braaied mushrooms
author: TASTE
ingredients: extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a griddle pan over a high heat.
Mix the mushrooms with the olive oil, oregano, lemon juice and garlic cloves. Season to taste.
Thread onto kebab sticks.
Grill in the pan or braai over medium coals until slightly charred.
Serve with toasted flour tortillas and a squeeze of lemon.

title: Bobotie with brown rice & lentils
author: Hannah Lewry
ingredients: 700 g free range lean beef mince
salt and freshly ground black pepper
120 g dried apricots, dried and chopped
steps: Sign in/Register

title: Biltong vleiskluitjies with soetmosterd
author: TASTE
ingredients: 3/4 cup cake flour, plus extra for dusting
oil or sunflower oil, for frying
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over a medium heat, then add the flour. Mix using a wooden spoon until incorporated. Add the milk and mix for 3 minutes.
Place a piece of clingwrap directly onto the surface of the mixture and chill.
Add the biltong sprinkle to the milk-and-flour mixture and mix. Return to the fridge.

Using 2 tablespoons, spoon a spoonful of the mixture into the extra flour. Coat it in the flour, then dip into the egg. Roll in the panko breadcrumbs, then return to the egg mixture and coat well before rolling in the breadcrumbs a second time.
Chill the dumplings while you heat the oil in a pan over a medium heat. Deep-fry the dumplings in batches for 30 seconds, or until golden brown and crispy. Drain on kitchen paper.
Serve with the spring onions and soetmosterd dressing.

title: Granola with yoghurt & berries
author: TASTE
steps: Place the nuts in a bowl, cover with warm filtered water and soak for 8 to 12 hours. Rinse well with cold water and dry, spread out on kitchen paper.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Roughly chop the nuts andcombine with the oats and cinnamon in a mixing bowl.
In a measuring cup, whisk together the honey, vanilla paste and coconut oil. Pour the oil-and-syrup mixture over the dry ingredients and mix well.
Line a baking tray with tinfoil and spread the granola mixture onto the tray. Bake for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally to ensure the mixture doesnât clump.
Remove from the oven, shake and stir, then allow to cool completely. The granola will crisp up as it cools.

title: French toast with strawberries
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1 vanilla pod, split and seeds scraped out
4 Tbsp sugar for the egg whites
4 Tbsp canola oil, plus extra for greasing
4 slices sourdough bread, sliced, to serve
steps: Beat the eggs with the vanilla seeds and sugar.
Heat the canola oil in a nonstick pan over a medium heat. Soak the bread in the egg for 2 minutes, then fry the egg-soaked bread for 3 minutes on each side.
Slice the strawberries and mix with therose-water, water and caster sugar. Steep for5 minutes, then spoon over the French toast.
Dust with icing sugar before serving.

title: Tangy coleslaw with a yoghurt dressing
ingredients: 100 g julienned carrots, cooked until soft
1 shredded large granny smith apple, sliced into 3 discs
1/2 lemon, cut into 8 slices for garnishing
steps: Combine all the salad ingredients in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, yoghurt, lemon juice and honey and pour over the salad.
Toss well and serve.

title: Strawberry & Bocconcini salad
author: TASTE
ingredients: A small handful coriander, finely chopped
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Mix the strawberries, pea shoots and cheese in a bowl. Pour over the dressing ( verjuice, coriander, red chilli, honey, olive oil, and sea salt and freshly ground pepper), toss and arrange on a plate.
Garnish with nasturtiums.

title: Iced beetroot & berry frappe
author: TASTE
steps: Sign in/Register

title: Pan-fried trout with Asian dressing
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1 x 400 g side lightly smoked trout, very thinly sliced
steps: Heat the olive oil in a pan over a high heat.
When hot, add the trout, skin side down, and fry for 1 minute. Turn and fry on the other side until just crisp and golden in colour.
Remove from the heat. Spoon the dressing (all ingredients except trout and olive oil) over the trout while it is still hot and serve immediately.

title: Strawberry & cream millefeuille
author: TASTE
ingredients: 500 g packets frozen butter puff pastry
steps: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Cut the slightly softened butter puff pastry into rectangles and lightly brush with beaten egg. Place on a preheated baking tray and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, or until puffed, golden and crispy.
Spoon some of the double cream onto a layer of pastry and top with sliced strawberries. Repeat with the remaining layers of pastry and strawberries, dust liberally with icing sugar and serve.

title: Raspberry fizz
author: TASTE
steps: Divide the raspberry liqueur and rose syrup between 4 glasses.
Fill the glasses with crushed ice and top up with tonic water.
Garnish with fresh raspberries and lime wedges.

title: Ready To Cook Roast Chicken
ingredients: 250ml castor sugar, plus extra for dipping the pastry shapes
30 ml canola oil, plus extra for greasing
shavings of pecorino or italian parmesan
5 ml sugar for the egg whites
1 x 400g can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Sign in/Register

title: Strawberry & prawn crystal rolls
author: TASTE
steps: Divide the ingredients for the filling into 8 portions. Soak 1 rice paper wrapper in warm water until it starts to soften a little, about 5 to 10 seconds. Lay the wrapper on a chopping board and place a portion of filling in the middle. Fold the bottom over the filling, fold in the sides and roll up. Repeat with the remaining rice paper wrappers and filling.
Serve with the chilli-pomegranate and coconut dipping sauces.

title: Vanilla pastry cups with mascarpone
author: TASTE
ingredients: 250 g flour, plus extra for dusting
3 Tbsp butter, plus extra, melted, for the tart base
1 vanilla pod, split and seeds scraped out
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Sift the flour onto a clean, dry work surface, then make a well in the flour and add the caster sugar, pushing it to the sides of the well.

Add the chopped butter, vanilla seeds and the egg yolks to the middle of the well and, using your fingertips, gently bring the mixture together to form a smooth dough. Knead until just combined, then wrap in clingwrap and chill for 30 minutes.

Roll out to a thickness of 3 mm, then cut into portions large enough to line the moulds of a greased muffin tray. Bake blind for 10 minutes. Remove the baking beans and bake for a further 5 minutes, or until golden. Allow to cool slightly before removing from the tray.
To serve, spoon a generous dollop of mascarpone into each pastry cup and top with a few blueberries before dusting liberally with icing sugar.

title: Madeleines with strawberry fizz
author: TASTE
ingredients: 225 g sugar for the egg whites
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. In a large mixing bowl, cream the sugar and butter until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs, one at a time, and mix to incorporate.
Add the vanilla extract and lemon zest, then fold in the flour to make a relatively dense dough.

Grease a madeleine tray and spoon the dough into the moulds, making sure to fill them completely. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, or until light golden and cooked through. Remove from the oven and allow to cool.
Whisk the icing sugar with a little water, adding more as you go if necessary, to make an icing with a sticky consistency. Drizzle liberally over the madeleines.

To make the strawberry fizz, purÃ©e 600 g strawberries with the liqueur and divide between 4 glasses or shallow dessert bowls. Quarter the remaining strawberries and scatter over the purÃ©e, then top up with the Prosecco just before serving.

title: Berry trifle
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1 cup cream, whipped, plus extra for serving
1x 200 g punnet, plus 10 husks on ripe gooseberries
steps: Sign in/Register

title: Crostini with bacon & strawberries
author: TASTE
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Thinly slice the ciabatta lengthways using a serrated knife. Arrange the slices on a baking tray, brush both sides with olive oil and season. Bake for 7 to 10 minutes, or until crispy and toasted.
Heat a frying pan over a high heat and fry the bacon until crispy.
Serve the crostini with the bacon, goatâs cheese, strawberries and balsamic cream. Garnish with mint or coriander microgreens.

title: Cranberry & hibiscus berry punch
steps: Combine the cranberry & hibiscus drinks with the soda water.
Add the berries and ice cubes and serve.

title: Sticky-sweet duck with blueberry
author: TASTE
steps: Preheat the oven to 150Â°C. Place the duck onto a baking tray and rub with olive oil, then top with the blueberries, drizzle with the honey and Port and add the vanilla pod.
Roast for 1 1/2â2 hours, basting occasionally, or until sticky and golden. Remove from the oven and leave to rest briefly, then portion and serve on a bed of crisp green beans on a large platter.

title: Raspberry & rose souffle
author: TASTE
ingredients: 2 Tbsp sugar for the egg whites
2 Tbsp cornflour, mixed with 2 1/2 Tbsp cold water
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. To make the rose coulis, dissolve the sugar in the water over a gentle heat. Add the rose petals and allow the syrup to infuse overnight.
Brush 4 small ramekins with the butter and dust with 30 g caster sugar, shaking out any excess sugar.
Place 300 g raspberries in a saucepan over a medium heat and cook for 5 minutes. Transfer to a blender and blend until smooth.

Strain the raspberries through a sieve. Discard the pips and return the purÃ©e to the saucepan. Simmer over a low heat. Add the lemon juice and 55 g sugar and stir until all the sugar has dissolved. Once the sugar has dissolved, bring to the boil.
Whisk the cornflour and water and add to the raspberry mixture. Whisk for 1 minute, then chill.
Beat the egg whites until soft peaks form. Slowly add the remaining caster sugar, beating continually. The meringue should be soft and glossy.
Fold in the raspberry purÃ©e and spoon into the ramekins. Bake for 10â13 minutes.
Remove the rose petals from the syrup. Crush the remaining raspberries, add 1 T rose syrup and mix. Pour over the souffles, dust with icing sugar and garnish with the crushed raspberries.

title: Sparkling lime-infused sangria
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1/2 ripe papaya, seeded, peeled and quartered
steps: Using a sharp mandolin, shred the radishes then toss with the caster sugar. Squeeze a little lime juice onto the rim of a pitcher and line with the sugared radish to create a frosted effect.

Fill the pitcher three-quarters full with the cucumber, strawberry, papaya, limes and cranberry juice and top up with soda water. Using a vegetable peeler, shave long ribbons of celery and asparagus, and use to decorate the pitcher. Serve chilled.

title: Mascarpone & berry tart
author: TASTE
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Place the puff pastry on a non-stick baking tray and spread with the mascarpone.
Sprinkle the treacle sugar over the mascarpone and bake for 20 minutes, or until the pastry is golden.
Place the strawberries and raspberries on the tart before serving.

title: Candied strawberry & chocolate shards
author: TASTE
steps: Sign in/Register

title: Eat In Indian Meals
ingredients: 1 loaf banana bread, sliced into 5mm slices
steps: Sign in/Register

title: Tropical fruit salad with avocado
author: TASTE
ingredients: 2 guavas, peeled and sliced into wedges
2 clementines, peeled and sliced into rings
A handful mint leaves, to serve
steps: Arrange the fruit on a serving platter. Drizzle over the granadilla pulp and lime juice.
Top with the avocado and sprinkle over the pistachios. Garnish with mint leaves and pour over the dressing just before serving.
To make the dressing, simmer the water and lemongrass in a small saucepan over a low heat until the water has reduced by a quarter. Remove from the heat and cool.
Remove the lemongrass and add the remaining ingredients. Whisk until combined.

title: Strawberry tarts
author: TASTE
ingredients: 2 tsp sugar for the egg whites
a pinch of sea salt, crushed, plus extra for topping
steps: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Cut out squares from the puff pastry. Use a fork to prick holes in the centre of each square. Chill for 30 minutes.
Place the strawberries, sugar and salt in a saucepan over a gentle heat and cook for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and chill for 30 minutes.
Bake the pastry squares for 5 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 180Â°C and bake until golden.
Layer the strawberries, chevin and rocket in the centre of each pastry square. Drizzle with balsamic crema before serving.

title: Avocado with poached egg
author: TASTE
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Bring the water and vinegar to the boil in a shallow saucepan.
Stir the water to create a whirlpool, then gently crack the eggs into the water.
Cook for 4 minutes for soft eggs.
Remove using a slotted spoon.
To serve, fill the avocado halves with hummus and top with the poached eggs.
Garnish with microgreens.

title: Seared coriander-crusted salmon
author: TASTE
ingredients: 2 red chillies, seeded and finely chopped (optional, to serve)
1 pear, thinly sliced and cut into matchsticks
40 g watercress leaves, tough stalks removed
steps: Pat the coriander seeds onto the salmon. Heat the butter and olive oil in a griddle pan. Sear the salmon, coriander side down, for 2 minutes.
Carefully turn over and cook skin side down for 3 minutes.
Remove from the heat and allow to cool slightly in the pan. Remove the skin by sliding an egg lifter between the skin and the flesh of the fish.
Place on a serving platter and serve with the salad.

To make the salad, combine the onion, dill, chilli and radish. Drizzle the pear and avocado with the lime or lemon juice. Combine with all the remaining salad ingredients except the watercress. Place the watercress on the sides of the fish and spoon the salad over the fish. Serve with the vinaigrette.

title: Tenderstem broccoli pesto
author: TASTE
ingredients: 4 Tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
a handful spring onions, chopped, to garnish
steps: Blend the broccoli, almonds, olive oil, garlic, Parmesan and lemon juice to a paste in a food processor or blender.
Season to taste.

title: Caesar- style tenderstem broccoli salad
author: TASTE
ingredients: 200 g Woolworths black pepper wood-smoked streaky bacon
130 g tenderstem broccoli tips, half raw and blanched
steps: Preheat the grill.
Place the bacon on a baking tray in a single layer and place under the heated grill.
Cook the bacon until crispy, then remove from the oven and allow to cool slightly.
Place the cubed bread onto the same tray and swirl to coat with the bacon fat.
Place under grill and toast until golden brown on both sides.
Remove from the oven and set aside.

title: Tenderstem broccoli and salad
ingredients: 130 g tenderstem broccoli tips, half raw and blanched
40 g watercress leaves, tough stalks removed
350 g strawberries, washed, hulled and sliced
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Sign in/Register

title: Bread and butter pudding
ingredients: fresh berries of your choice, to serve
200 g butter, plus extra, melted, for the tart base
slow roasted fresh berries, to garnish
steps: Sign in/Register

title: Blueberry & coconut semifreddo
author: TASTE
ingredients: 2 Tbsp sugar for the egg whites
50 g desiccated coconut + extra for sprinkling
200 g sugar for the egg whites
steps: To make the semifreddo, place the blueberries, sugar and water in a saucepan and gently simmer until blueberries are soft.
PurÃ©e the blueberries in a blender and strain. Discard the blueberry skins and seeds. Chill for approximately 30 minutes.
Line a bowl with clingwrap, allowing it to hang over the edges of the bowl.

Place the eggs, egg yolk and caster sugar in another bowl over a saucepan of simmering water. Using a hand beater, beat the mixture until pale and thick. Remove from the heat and continue beating until the mixture is cool.
Place the cream and coconut cream in a bowl and whisk until soft peaks form. Gently fold the cream into the egg mixture.
Pour the blueberry purÃ©e into the bowl, then top with the egg mixture. Freeze overnight.
To make the lemongrass syrup, gently heat the sugar and water in a saucepan until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat, add the lemongrass and allow to infuse for 1 hour.
To make the coconut-andpistachio brittle, lay the pistachios and toasted coconut on a baking tray.

Gently heat the sugar and water in a saucepan over a low heat until the sugar has melted. Bring the mixture to the boil and reduce the syrup until it turns a golden caramel colour (watch carefully as it will burn quickly).
Pour the caramel over the pistachios and coconut and allow to cool and set.
To serve, turn the semifreddo out onto a platter, drizzle over the strained lemongrass syrup and garnish with the coconut-and pistachio brittle and fresh blueberries.

title: Aubergine, tomato and mozzarella stacks
ingredients: 2 x 350  g brinjals, cut into wedges
steps: Pre-heat the oven to 200Â°c.
Heat a saucepan over medium heat then sautÃ© the onion in a splash of olive oil until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, peppers and herbs and allow to fry for another 5 minutes then add the tomatoes and tomato paste.
Lower the heat and allow to simmer for 10-15 minutes until the vegetables are soft and fragrant.
Season to taste and remove from the heat.
To make the roasted aubergines, place the aubergine slices on a roasting tray then drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Place in the oven and allow to roast for 15-20 minutes until they are golden brown and almost cooked through.
Layer the aubergine slices with tomato sauce and slices of mozzarella then place back in the oven and allow to bake for 5 minutes until the mozzarella melts.
Remove from the oven then serve with fresh basil leaves.

title: Coconut-chia seed pudding
author: TASTE
steps: Soak the chia seeds in the coconut milk overnight in the fridge.

Mix the yoghurt and white chocolate and chill. Preheat the oven to 125Â°C. Remove the leaves from the strawberries, keeping the stems intact. Place on a baking tray in a single layer. Slow roast in the oven for 60â90 minutes, then allow to cool. Drizzle with a little honey if you like. Reserve strawberry pan juices.

Spoon the mixed berries into the bottom of a glass bowl. Spoon over the white chocolate yoghurt and top with the slowroasted strawberries and the coconut-chia mixture. Drizzle with the strawberry pan juices before serving.

title: Crumbed chicken with veggie lasagne bake
ingredients: 2 x 375 ml sundried tomato and pecorino pasta sauce
1 x 600 g Easy to cook chicken fillets with mozzarella
1 red onion, cut into thin petals
salt and freshly ground black pepper
Cooked sweet potato with cinnamon butter
steps: Prepare the easy bake chicken fillets as per the instructions and serve with the veggie lasagne.

For the lasagne, add some sauce to the bottom of an oven proof roasting dish followed by a sheet of the blanched lasagne pasta.Add some marrow, sweet potato, onion and spinach followed by salt, pepper and garlic and herb spice.Drizzle over the cheese sauce and cover with another lasagne sheet and repeating the process until all the sheets and veggies are used.Finish with some cheese sauce before covering with foil and cooking in the oven for 30 minutes and the marrow is tender.
Remove the foil and cook for another 10 minute until the cheese is slightly browned.

title: Spicy tomato meatballs
ingredients: 1/2 cup medium red onions, thinly sliced
steps: For the meatballs, combine all the ingredients then mix well.
Form golf-ball sized meatballs and fry in a large, hot frying pan until browned all over but still raw inside.
Remove from the pan and set aside.
To make the tomato sauce, fry the onion in a saucepan until soft and translucent then add the garlic, chilli flakes and paprika.
Add the tomatoes then break up with a potato masher and add the tomato paste. Fill the tin the tomatoes came in half with water and add to the pot then add the xylitol.
Lower the heat and allow to simmer for 10-15 minutes until reduced slightly.
Season to taste then drop in the meatballs and allow to simmer gently for 10 minutes until the meatballs are cooked but still juicy.
In the meantime, break the cauliflower heads up into florets and pulse in a food processor until finely chopped and resembling couscous.

Heat a large frying pan over high heat then saute the onion in the butter/olive oil until soft. Add the cauliflower couscous and the stock then allow to simmer for 10-15 minutes until the cauliflower is cooked through but still keeping its shape.
Season to taste then serve with the spicy tomato meatballs.

title: Venison burger with caramelised apples
steps: To make the caramelised apples, heat a large, non-stick frying pan over medium heat then sautÃ© the apples and onions until they are golden brown.
Add the sugar, sherry vinegar and salt and allow to caramelise until the apples and onions are sticky. Remove from the heat and set aside.
To make the burger patties, fry the onion and garlic in a frying pan until soft and golden brown then mix with the venison mince, breadcrumbs, egg, herbs and spices.
Divide the mixture into 4 and form into burgers.
Fry the burgers in a large frying pan/griddle pan until cooked to  your preference.
30 seconds before the burgers are done, place the sliced mature cheddar on top and allow to soften slightly.
To serve, top the toasted buns with mayo and mustard, salad leaves, burger patties and finally a generous spoonful of the caramelised apples and onions.
Serve immediately.

title: Venison steak tacos
ingredients: 120 g dried apricots, dried and chopped
sea salt and pepper to taste
a pinch sea salt, plus extra to taste
steps: To make the apricot-habanero cream, place the diced apricots and chillies into a small bowl and cover with boiling water.
Allow to stand for 10 minutes to soften.
When the apricots are soft, drain and blend with the crÃ¨me fraiche, lemon juice, salt and pepper with a hand blender. Set aside.
Heat a griddle pan over high heat.
Drizzle the olive oil and Balsamic vinegar over the steaks then season to taste with the salt and pepper.
Grill the steaks for 3-4 minutes per side until the steaks are medium rare.
Remove from the grill and allow to rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Season the cabbage and avo with fresh lemon juice, salt and pepper.
To assemble the tacos, heat/toast the tacos over an open flame then top with the shredded cabbage, avocado slices, steak strips and finally the apricot-habanero cream.
Serve immediately.

title: Venison hot dog with beetroot relish
ingredients: 1/2 cup medium red onions, thinly sliced
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: To make the relish, fry the onion in a splash of olive oil until soft and translucent.
Add the cubed beetroot, Balsamic vinegar, brown sugar, salt and pepper and allow to cook gently for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and set aside to cool slightly.
Cook the sausage in a hot frying pan or on the braai until done to your preference.
To serve, slice the sausage and place inside the toasted hot dog rolls. Top with a generous spoonful of the beetroot relish and finish with a sprinkling of micro rocket leaves.

title: Green tomato & watermelon salad
author: TASTE
ingredients: A handful micro herbs, for serving
a pinch sea salt, plus extra to taste
steps: Slice or cut the tomatoes into wedges, depending on their size. Place in a large salad bowl. Cut the flesh of the watermelon into large chunks and add to the dish along with the red chilli.
Scatter over the pomegranate rubies and garnish with the microleaf salad and edible flowers. Drizzle over the dressing before serving.
To make the tomato seed dressing, squeeze the juice and seeds of the tomatoes into a mixing bowl. Add the olive oil, balsamic vinegar, garlic, honey and salt and whisk.

title: Raw beetroot-and-fig salad
author: TASTE
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
A handful micro herbs, for serving
steps: Wash, peel and thinly slice beetroot and feta cheese. Half the figs and drizzle with oil oil
Garnish with pomegranate seeds, micro herbs and edible flowers.
Season to taste

title: Chia vanilla pudding
steps: Combine the chia sees, vanilla, almond milk and honey in a bowl and stir well.
Cover with clingwrap and place in the fridge to allow the chia seeds to soak and swell overnight.
When the chia seeds have absorbed all the liquid, transfer to serving dishes then top with whipped cream and fresh raspberries and serve.

title: Mediterranean prawns & barley salad
author: TASTE
ingredients: 150 g red speckled beans, soaked overnight
1/2 cup medium red onions, thinly sliced
A small handful coriander, finely chopped
4 Tbsp red wine vinegar, to serve
1 tsp italian parsley or micro herbs, chopped
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
500 g Prawns, shells & heads removed & deveined
steps: Cook the beans and barley according to package instructions and cool. Combine the onion, chilli, coriander, vinegar, olive oil, garlic and parsley and toss with the beans and barley. Season to taste.
To make the Mediterranean prawns, heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the prawns on both sides until cooked through. Mix the pine nuts with the paprika.
Spoon the barley-and-bean salad onto plates. Top with the asparagus, tomatoes, avocado and prawns. Scatter over the pine nuts and serve with the limes.

title: Moroccan red & white quinoa salad
author: TASTE
ingredients: fresh fruit such as figs, plums, berries or peaches, to garnish
A handful Pomegranate rubies, to serve
1/2 cup medium red onions, thinly sliced
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Cook the quinoa according to package instructions and cool.
Mix the cooled quinoa with the cumin, coriander, lemon juice and season with salt and pepper to taste. Drizzle with a little olive oil and chill.

To make the beetroot pickle dressing, cover the stems of the beetroot with small pieces of foil. Place the vinegar, water, sugar, star anise and cinnamon in a deep saucepan. Place the beetroot upright in the liquid and simmer for 30â40 minutes, or until the beetroot starts to soften. Remove from the heat. Remove the beetroot from the liquid and peel when cool enough to handle. Set aside. Add the onion and radish to the beetroot liquid and soak until cool. Remove the onion and radish from the liquid and chill.

Return the remaining beetroot liquid to the heat and simmer until reduced to Â½ cup . Remove the star anise and cinnamon stick. Add the pomegranate syrup and season to taste. Remove from the heat and cool. Place the feta into the reduction and marinate for 2â3 hours, turning once. Remove and roll in the toasted sunflower seeds.
Heat a little sunflower oil in a pan and fry the sliced brinjal on both sides until golden brown and cooked through. Drizzle with a little pomegranate dressing and roll up. Season to taste.

To serve, roll the beetroot in the chia seeds. Place all the ingredients on a platter with the quinoa in the centre. Garnish with pomegranate rubies and pumpkin seeds and drizzle with the beetroot pickle dressing.

title: Phyllo cheese strips
author: TASTE
ingredients: 100 g plain greek style feta, crumbled
160 g parmesan cheese, grated, plus extra for dusting
1 x 250 g tub mascarpone, for serving
a crack of black pepper to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 190Â°C. Sandwich 2 sheets of phyllo pastry with olive oil. Cut in half lengthways.
To make the cheese paste, mash: feta, Parmesan, chevin and mascarpone together in a bowl.
Spread a third of the cheese paste on one half. Cover with the other half, pressing down to seal.
Slice into strips. Place on a baking sheet lined with baking paper. Brush lightly with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Repeat until you have used all the pastry.
Bake until golden and crisp â about 8 minutes, but start checking after 5 minutes to ensure they donât overcook.

title: Meringue medallions with berries
author: TASTE
steps: Preheat the oven to 110Â°C. Beat the egg whites with the cream of tartar until soft peaks form. Gradually beat in the sugar, then beat until stiff and glossy. Fold in the vanilla and vinegar.
Line large baking trays with baking paper. Spread thin rounds of meringue mixture onto the baking paper â some small, some a little larger â I like them different sizes.
Bake for 1 hour. Turn off the heat and leave to cool in the oven.
Spread with mascarpone and stud with berries and layer to make a tower if you like.

title: Beetroot-cured salmon
author: TASTE
steps: Place the salmon on a stainless-steel tray, skin-side down.
Mix the caster sugar, sea salt, peppercorns, orange juice and zest and dill.
Grate the beetroot into the sugar mixture.
Spread the mixture over the fish and massage into the fish. Wrap the fish in clingfilm and place a heavy weight, such as canned food, on top. Allow to stand overnight.
Pour off and discard any excess liquid. Remove the clingfilm and scrape off the cure and discard.
Thinly slice the fish just before serving with the capers, lemon-dressed leaves, crÃ¨me fraÃ®che and fresh bread.

title: Slow-roasted tomato salad
author: TASTE
ingredients: 2 Tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
steps: Preheat the oven to 120Â°C and bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil.
Cut a cross into the base of each Roma tomato and blanch in the salted water for 30 seconds, then refresh in ice-cold water. Peel each tomato, then place the peeled tomatoes in a bowl.
Add the salt and caster sugar and mix well to coat each tomato thoroughly.
Place the Roma tomatoes on a greased baking tray and roast for 1â2 hours, or until dehydrated.
To make the dressing, combine the tahini and garlic, then slowly whisk in the lemon juice, olive oil, honey and sherry vinegar. Add the sesame seeds and mix.
To assemble, place the halved exotic tomatoes and the slow-roasted Roma tomatoes on a plate and spoon over the tahini dressing. Season with salt and extra sesame seeds.

title: Vibrant broad beans with asparagus
author: TASTE
ingredients: 20 g Parmesan, grated, plus extra for sprinkling
1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
steps: Blanch the asparagus in boiling salted water for 1 minute, then refresh in ice-cold water. Do the same with the broad beans, then remove the skins.
To make the dip, blend the asparagus, peas, chevin, anchovies and Parmesan until creamy. Add the lemon juice and mix through.
To serve, drizzle the broad beans with olive oil and season with salt. Serve with the asparagus dip and garnish with pea shoots and extra grated Parmesan.

title: Pea, feta and mint falafel
author: TASTE
ingredients: 4 Tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
1/2 cup medium red onions, thinly sliced
A handful torn fresh mint leaves
100 g plain greek style feta, crumbled
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
a handful of organic pistachios, roughly chopped, for garnishing
2 tbs fresh coriander, finely chopped (plus extra as garnish)
steps: Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Add the peas, bring back to the boil and cook for 1 minute, then drain and allow to cool slightly.
Heat 2 T oil in a pan over a medium heat. Add the onion, chilli, cumin and sesame seeds and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until softened. Allow to cool.

Spoon the onion mixture into a food processor, then add the peas, mint, egg, breadcrumbs and the feta. Blitz to create a coarse paste. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Allow the mixture to rest for 20 minutes.
Working with slightly damp hands, shape 1 T of the mixture into a mini patty. Repeat with the remaining mixture to make 16 rounds.
Heat 2 T oil in a pan and cook the falafels in batches in single layers for 3â4 minutes until golden. Add more oil as necessary.
To make the dressing, combine: plain yoghurt, lemon juice, coriander, garlic, 1 tsp mint, and nutmeg
Warm the pitas, cut into wedges and top with the warm falafel, pickled cabbage, yoghurt dressing, pistachios, mint and pink peppercorns.

title: Golden toffee apples
author: TASTE
ingredients: 400 g sugar for the egg whites
4 large granny smith apple, sliced into 3 discs
steps: Heat the sugar and water in a saucepan over a medium heat. Allow the sugar to dissolve and the mixture to reach a gentle boil.
The sugar should start to brown after boiling for 5 minutes.
Once it turns a golden colour, dip the base of the saucepan into iced water to stop the sugar from browning too much.
Skewer the apples using long kebab sticks. Dip the apples into the toffee and turn to coat well. Hold over the saucepan to allow the excess toffee to drip off.
Place the toffee apples on a silicone baking mat and allow them to harden before removing the sticks.
Once cooled, arrange on a platter and serve.

title: Caramelised pineapple
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1 pineapples,with stems, peeled and each cut into 6 wedges
2 x 80 g small pieces white chocolate
steps: Heat the sugar and butter in a pan over a medium heat. Once the sugar begins to melt, swirl the pan, then add the pineapple.
Allow the pineapple to caramelise for 2 minutes, then turn and cook the other side. Once both sides are cooked, remove from the pan and allow to cool slightly.
To make the white chocolate ganache, melt the chocolate and cream in a bowl over a saucepan of just simmering water. Remove from the heat and stir until smooth.
Serve with the caramelised pineapple and garnish with the gold-dusted bay leaves.

title: Five-spice pomegranate-glazed gammon
author: TASTE
ingredients: 1 cup Verlaque five-spice Persian pomegranate concentrate
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Rub the gammon with olive oil and sprinkle with sea salt.
Cook in the oven for 30 minutes per 500 g plus an extra 30 minutes. When cooked through, carefully remove the rind and score the fat in a crisscross pattern.
Coat in the five-spice pomegranate syrup, then return the meat to the oven until the fat crisps up and almost caramelises.
Leave the gammon to rest for 15 minutes and carve into thin slivers.

title: Camembert tower with butterscotch
author: TASTE
ingredients: 200 g sugar for the egg whites
3/4 cup sugar for the egg whites
100 g pecan nuts, toasted and roughly chopped
steps: To make the butterscotch sauce, heat 200g sugar in a pan over a medium heat until caramelised. Don't stir â rather swirl the pan to evenly melt the sugar.
Add 85g butter once the sugar is light golden brown in colour. Swirl to combine. Once the butter has melted into the sugar, remove the pan from the heat and pour in the cream and stir.

To make the sugar shards, melt 1 cup of sugar in the same way as for the butterscotch sauce. Once the sugar is light golden in colour, pour onto a silicone baking mat. Sprinkle over the chopped nuts before the sugar sets.
Once the sugar has set, break it into shards.
Layer the sugar shards between the Camembert rounds and stack to form a tower.
Drizzle over the butterscotch sauce before serving.

title: Orange marmalade & ginger glazed gammon
author: TASTE
steps: Place the gammon in a large cast-iron saucepan. Add the ginger beer and simmer gently on a medium to low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes, adding a little water if necessary. Remove the gammon from the saucepan and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 160Â°C.
Remove the rind from the gammon and discard, then score the fat and rub with oil. Meanwhile, place a small saucepan over a medium to low heat and add the marmalade and candied ginger.
Heat until reduced and runny. Brush the gammon with the glaze then arrange on a baking tray and roast for 15 minutes, or until crisp and sticky-sweet. Leave to rest for 5 minutes before carving.

title: Mushroom crostini
author: TASTE
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Stir-fry the mushrooms in olive oil over a high heat until all the liquid has evaporated.Mix the mushrooms with the remaining ingredients.
To make the crostini, preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Thinly slice the panini or baguette and toast for 5 to 10 minutes, or until golden brown.
Spoon the mushroom mixture onto the crostini and serve immediately.

title: Olive & bacon tartlets
author: TASTE
steps: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Cut out circles of phyllo pastry, lightly brush with melted butter and arrange in a greased muffin pan. Bake for 5 to 10 minutes, or until golden.
Combine chopped Rosa tomatoes, black olive tapenade,  chopped flat-leaf parsley, crushed black olives and seasoning, to taste, if necessary.
Fry rashers bacon in a hot pan until crispy, then spoon the olive mixture into the phyllo pastry cups and top with crispy bacon.

title: Cranberry & apple glazed gammon
author: TASTE
ingredients: 120 g pillow pack oganic crisp lettuce
400 g Asparagus, blanched and cut on the diagonal
steps: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.
Add the cranberry-and-apple jam to a small saucepan, and reduce over a low heat for 5 minutes, or until a thin syrup forms.
Place the gammon on a tinfoil-lined tray and glaze with the cranberry-and-apple syrup. Roast for 1 hour, or until the fat is golden and slightly crisp.

Melt the butter in a large pan over a medium-high heat. Using a cookie-cutter, cut the apple slices into star shapes. Place in the pan, with the blueberries and brown sugar, and fry until plump and caramelised.
Mash the ripe avocados with the lemon juice, olive oil and seasoning. Toss with the salad leaves, until the latter are coated in the creamy dressing.
Slice the blanched greens in half lengthways and serve with portions of oven-roasted gammon garnished with the caramelised-apple stars and blueberries.
Place the creamy salad leaves in a separate bowl and serve on the side, with ramekins of English-mustard mayonnaise.

title: Spinach & feta snack pies
author: TASTE
ingredients: 250ml feta cheese, crumbled, plus extra to serve
flaky salt and ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.
Press excess moisture from the spinach and chop roughly. Mix spinach with dill and feta cheese. Season.
Halve the pastry. Place half the filling down the middle of each sheet.
Fold pastry into two âsausageâ rolls, bake for 15 minutes and turn the oven down to 180Â°C.
Bake until pastry is crisp and golden. Allow to cool slightly before slicing with a sharp knife.
Sprinkle with toasted seeds.
Serve as a snack with drinks, or on the side with a soup.

title: Crispy potato cakes with salmon
author: TASTE
ingredients: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Add the potatoes to a saucepan and submerge. Cook over a high heat in rapidly boiling water until tender. Drain, then mash the warm potatoes with the cream and butter, adding a little of both at a time until the mixture is creamy and lump free. Season to taste.

Add the egg and mix. Using your hands, mould into thick patties. Add Â½ cup canola oil to a pan and place over a medium to high heat. When the oil is hot, dust the potato cakes with flour and fry on each side until crisp and golden.

Drain on paper towel. Repeat until all the cakes are fried â if the oil becomes dirty, clean the pan and use the remaining oil. Top each potato cake with shavings of goatâs-milk cheddar and drape with a slice of smoked salmon. Top with slivers of red onion and scatter with snipped chives and fennel fronds. Season to taste and serve.

title: Chicken liver pate with pomegranate
author: TASTE
ingredients: 2 x 125 g tubs chicken liver pÃ¢tÃ©
70 g baby cos lettuce, for serving
steps: Place the chicken-liver pÃ¢tÃ© in the freezer for 15 minutes. Un-mould and slice into thick pieces. Sprinkle each side with pistachio nuts.
Heat a nonstick pan until hot then quickly sear each piece. Keep warm in the oven until all the pieces have been seared.
Place on a few baby cos lettuce leaves, scatter over the strawberries and drizzle with the warmed pomegranate concentrate.
Serve with extra-long breadsticks.

title: Ultimate roast turkey
steps: Use the melted butter and a brush and paint the sage leaves onto the turkey. Season with salt and freshly cracked black pepper.
Cook turkey according to pack instructions.

Remove turkey from roasting pan and use a large spoon to scoop the top layer of oil off. Pour the pan juices through a strainer and into a small saucepan. Simmer to reduce a little and add the cranberries and fig glaze.
Reduce heat and simmer to a thick consistency, but do not burn. Remove from heat and add port. Stir trough and spoon over the turkey and keep some to serve on the side.

title: Crisp pan roasted potatoes with rosemary
ingredients: 4 Tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
steps: Boil the potatoes in salt water until they start to soften.
Remove from heat. Add oil into a large skillet and bring to a medium heat.
Cut potatoes in quarters and shallow fry until crisp and golden brown on all sides while turning with tongs.
Add rosemary towards the end of the cooking process to the pan.
Remove from heat and sprinkle with Malden salt. Serve immediately.

title: Beef carpaccio & beetroot mayonnaise
ingredients: 1 x 500 g seared pepper crusted beef fillet
4 raw beetroot, thinly sliced & pressed out with a star shaped cookie cutter
3/4 cup plus 2 tsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
steps: Cover the seared fillet tightly with aluminum foil and roll into a log shape.
Place in the fridge for 2-3 hours. Remove just before serving and slice thinly with a slicer or serrated knife.

To make the mayonnaise: Lightly beat the eggs in a blender, then add lemon juice, garlic and mustard and beat to combine. Continue beating, adding a drop of oil at a time. Gradually add more oil and whisk until thick and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Blend the left-over beetroot pieces into a paste and strain the beetroot juice using a fine sieve. Mix a few drops into the mayonnaise, adding more if itâs too thick.
Serve the beef on individual plates or on a large platter.
Top with beetroot, sliced onion, drained radishes and drizzle with the beetroot mayonnaise.
Serve with salad leaves and edible flowers.

title: A three course ginger infused menu
ingredients: 300 g dark chocolate, chopped and melted
2.5 kg free range leg of lamb
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
steps: Sign in/Register

title: Christmas ice cream cake
ingredients: 1 plain fruit cake, sliced into 12 slices but kept together
100 g cherries, halved and washed under hot running water then drained and dusted with flour
steps: Use a loose-bottomed cake pan and lay the fruit cake piece by piece to complete a full layer â using slices will make it easier to cut through the frozen ice cream cake later.
Smear with pistachio ice cream. Do the same with the second cake.
Top with a layer of strawberry ice cream and place in freezer overnight.
